problem.claim: Whether softmax-attention Chain-of-Thought transformers are Turing-complete.

gap.claim: Turing-completeness was known for hard-attention CoT transformers, but remained open for softmax-attention CoT transformers.

contributions.claim: Proves that length-generalizable softmax CoT transformers are Turing-complete via the CoT extension of Counting RASP.
Establishes Turing-completeness for CoT C-RASP with causal masking over unary and, more generally, letter-bounded languages.
Shows that relative positional encoding extends the construction to arbitrary languages, whereas the unextended system is not Turing-complete there.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors characterize length-generalizable softmax CoT transformers as Turing-complete, presenting this as a stronger result.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report proving Turing-completeness for the specified CoT C-RASP settings and for the relative-position extension on arbitrary languages.
The authors report empirical validation by training transformers on various languages requiring complex, non-linear arithmetic reasoning.

narrative_sequence.summary: Hard-attention CoT transformers are described as already known to be Turing-complete.
The abstract identifies softmax-attention CoT transformers as an unresolved case.
The paper claims a stronger result for length-generalizable softmax CoT transformers, using CoT C-RASP as the proof route.

The result is established first for causal masking on unary or letter-bounded languages, then extended to arbitrary languages with relative positional encoding; the unextended arbitrary-language case is reported as not Turing-complete.
Training experiments on languages requiring complex non-linear arithmetic reasoning are reported as empirical validation.

source_observation.claim: The abstract states the main theorem through an intermediate formalism and explicitly separates language-scope restrictions from the relative-position extension.

lessons.interpretation: A compact theorem claim becomes more informative when its proof vehicle, domain of validity, and boundary cases are named together.
lessons.application: State a theoretical result with the intermediate representation used, the exact input-language scope, and any extension needed to reach the broader claim.
lessons.exception: This structure is less useful when the paper has no formal intermediary or when scope distinctions are immaterial to the result.

unknowns: The abstract gives no proof details, construction, theorem conditions beyond the stated masking and language scopes, or formal definition of length generalization.
The empirical report omits datasets, baselines, training procedures, metrics, and quantitative results.
